reason: The published once@1.4.0 documents once.proto() but fails to export it. Upstream committed and signed v1.4.1 with the missing export and a regression test, yet npm still has no 1.4.1 artifact. The small CommonJS surface can be characterized exactly, the published wrapper also mishandles callback properties that collide with its public called/value state, no maintained drop-in preserves strict/proto/state semantics, and two distinct active direct consumers provide a tested migration-PR path and a genuine maintainer-decision issue path.
problem: once@1.4.0 assigns proto to the inner once function after exporting wrappy(once), so consumers receive only the callable default and strict exports. Its wrappy integration also copies caller callback properties after initializing wrapper state; a callback with an own called=true or value property can suppress its first invocation or expose a value before invocation.

successorLandscape.onetime: onetime@8 is ESM-only, requires Node >=22, and does not preserve once.strict, once.proto, wrapper.called or wrapper.value as a drop-in contract.

successorLandscape.decision: A small provenance-locked continuation has distinct compatibility value.

compatibilityContract: Callable CommonJS root export usable through direct scoped installation and npm alias under the historical once key
Root once(fn) executes fn once with unchanged this, arguments and return identity, then returns the cached value
once.strict(fn) throws on every call after the first and preserves the historical named error wording
Wrapper public called and value state before, during and after synchronous execution, re-entry and throws
Own enumerable callback decorations are copied without allowing called, value or onceError collisions to corrupt internal state
once.proto() is exported as a one-time initializer and installs configurable non-enumerable Function.prototype.once and onceStrict methods with historical descriptor and error behavior
Historical deep entry once/once.js and scoped @stackline/once/once.js remain available
No Node-only APIs; CommonJS and ordinary ESM-to-CJS interop work in Node and browser bundlers
No runtime dependency is required if the wrappy behavior can be reproduced with reserved-state safety
risk: The code is small but function wrappers expose subtle observable state, property-copying, re-entry, thrown-error, prototype-mutation and descriptor behavior. A compatibility regression can silently skip callbacks.

pullRequest.plan: Use once as the historical dependency key with an npm alias to @stackline/once, add a focused callback-property regression, and run the repository's complete clean test/lint gates.
pullRequest.concreteBenefit: Restify wraps caller-provided callbacks. The published wrappy path can copy an own called=true/value decoration over fresh wrapper state and suppress the first callback; the maintained replacement reserves its state keys while preserving other decorations.
